messages:
emily_acme: Hey team — running into a weird rerank behaviour. I POST to /v1/rerank and the returned scores are all 0 or some candidates are missing. I think it might be an input shape issue. Example curl body I send:

emily_acme: ```json
{
  "query": "best payment flow",
  "documents": [
    {"id": "p1", "text": "How to set up payment", "metadata": {"type":"guide"}},
    {"id": "p2", "text": "Payment UX tips"}
  ]
}
```

alex_cs: Thanks for the snippet, Emily. Are you hitting the hosted API with raw HTTP or via one of the SDKs? Also which model exactly?

emily_acme: Raw HTTP, curl from our CI job. Using model=rnd-rerank-v1, auth header with our service key.

maria_support: Quick note: our public examples for the rerank endpoint use the field name `candidates` rather than `documents`. If you send `documents` the server currently attempts a best-effort parse and may fall back to an older codepath which can produce 0 scores or drop entries. Can you try renaming to `candidates`?

emily_acme: I tried swapping to `candidates` and now I get a 400: "Malformed candidates: expected array of strings or objects with top-level text". Our objects do have a `text` field though — we usually have `passages` nested inside each document.

sam_eng: Reproduced locally. The rerank API expects `candidates` to be either an array of strings OR an array of objects where the candidate's text lives in the top-level `text` key (i.e., `{id, text, metadata}`). It does NOT traverse `passages` or nested arrays. Also it expects `query` as the query key — `q` is not supported. If you send `{documents: [...]}` the server currently doesn't return a specific schema error, it can end up scoring a blank input.

emily_acme: Ah — our ingestion pipeline emits docs shaped like `{id, passages: [{text, start, end}, ...], metadata}`. We assumed the server would find the first passage automatically. What's the recommended approach for multi-passage documents?

sam_eng: Short answer: expand passages client-side. Rerank treats each candidate as an atomic unit to rank. If you want passage-level ranking, flatten each passage into its own candidate and include an id that preserves parent doc context, e.g. `doc123::p2`. If you need to return doc-level scores, you can aggregate passage scores on the client.

emily_acme: That's annoying for large docs but doable. Any limits we should watch when flattening?

alex_cs: Current limits: max candidates per request = 1000 (we'll add to docs), request payload size also enforced. Also note that if both `documents` and `candidates` are present, the service will prefer `candidates` and ignore `documents` silently for now. We'll make that behavior explicit + more helpful errors.

maria_support: Filed internal ticket INF-4523 to improve schema validation and return 4xx with hints when ambiguous keys are used.

rerank-bot: INF-4523 created by maria_support: "rerank: ambiguous input keys (documents vs candidates) -> add schema validation + hint"

emily_acme: Can you share a minimal working payload example for the flattened passages approach so I can change our pipeline quickly?

sam_eng: Sure — working example that ranks passages individually:

sam_eng: ```json
{
  "query": "best payment flow",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"p1::1","text":"How to set up payment"},
    {"id":"p1::2","text":"Payment integration examples"},
    {"id":"p2::1","text":"Payment UX tips"}
  ]
}
```

alex_cs: For debugging you can also add `?explain=true` to the rerank endpoint to get back token-level or per-candidate scoring details (explain enabled for enterprise/debug keys only). That helped us triage similar cases.

emily_acme: That worked — scores now look sensible after flattening. Two follow-ups: 1) any plan to accept `passages` nested inside each document? 2) can we get clearer errors when user sends `documents` instead of `candidates`?

sam_eng: We're planning to add stricter schema validation and clearer errors per INF-4523. Passage-first support is tracked under INF-4590 (feature request to accept nested passages and auto-flatten with limits). No ETA yet. We'll prioritize docs and examples first.

maria_support: I'll push a docs PR with examples for both string candidates and object candidates, and add a small helper script to flatten passages. Will ping Emily when deployed.

emily_acme: Awesome — appreciate the quick turn. Will test the flatten script and report back if anything else pops up. :raised_hands:

alex_cs: Thanks for reporting, Emily. We'll follow up on INF-4523 and INF-4590. If you hit rate/latency errors while flattening, ping support and we'll scope a dedicated flow.

emily_acme: Will do — cheers!
